messages:
sam: Quick sync — I kicked off replay vs synth runs on the new gpubase:cuda-12.1 image and noticed ~12% tail latency regression vs the benchmark image we used last month. Is anyone else seeing kernel-selector differences when driver/libcudnn versions change?
akash: Yep, saw similar on Friday. Short version: same model + same batch config picked different GEMM kernels on A100 vs A100 (driver mismatch felt subtle).
maria: Can you paste the exact image tags and the driver/cuda versions? We should confirm ABI-level parity.
sam: Image tags: gpubase:cuda-12.1-rt-v3 (the new one) vs bench-image:cuda-12.1-rt-v1. Drivers: host 525.85 vs 525.89 on the bench infra. libcudnn: 8.9.2 vs 8.9.2 (same).
akash: Small diffs in driver patch can flip cuBLAS heuristics. Also check TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST and any CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES remapping.
perf-bot: perf-run: replay harness (1765432100). aggregate p50/p95/p99: bench-image {p50: 18ms, p95: 55ms, p99: 120ms} vs gpubase {p50: 20ms, p95: 62ms, p99: 135ms}. KV cache miss rate 0.6% higher on gpubase.
jit: I captured a short nvprof/nsight run — looks like different kernel names for MatMul: "cublasLt_matmul_f32_128x256" vs "cublasLt_matmul_f32_64x128" selection. Smaller tile caused more kernel launches.
olivia: Could batching heuristics be interacting? If kernel latency scales poorly, our dynamic batching window might trigger more frequent flushes. Are you using the same BATCH_WINDOW_MS / MAX_BATCH_TOKENS?
sam: Yes, identical batching config. Also confirmed our runtime binary is identical (sha256). Only container userspace libs differ.
akash: Then focus on CUDA/driver toolchain. Two practical steps: (1) collect cuobjdump / cupti traces to see chosen kernels, (2) run a controlled microbench for single-matmul shapes used in long-tail requests.
maria: Also check LD_LIBRARY_PATH ordering — sometimes vendor libs in the image shadow host libs at runtime (rdms). Could cause different cublasLt fallback paths.
ci-bot: ci:repro job queued — repro-runner/1765432120. Will produce a minimal docker-compose reproducer with NV_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0.
sam: I reproduced with a minimal replay harness (attached in thread) — there is a subtle memcpy spike before the KV restore step on the gpubase image.  snippet: ```text
[  memcopy ]  src: host -> device  size: 2.4MB  latency: 1.2ms (gpubase) vs 0.4ms (bench-image)
```
jit: That memcpy hit could explain the higher p99. Where is the memcpy coming from? KV prefetch turned on? Check PREFETCH_KV=true in runtime env.
olivia: Our recent KV change introduced a prefetch path guarded by PREFETCH_KV. Maybe gpubase pulled in a different libc that changed malloc alignment -> different pinned allocation behavior. If host to device copies are not pinned, cudaMemcpy is async/slow.
akash: Repro checklist for apples-to-apples: same GPU model, same host driver major+minor, identical container base (glibc, libstdc++), same TORCH/CUDA env vars, same LD_LIBRARY_PATH ordering, same kernel flags (no weird MIG settings), same NUMA/cpuset. Also ensure NVIDIA persistence daemon config is same.
maria: I'll run cuMemGetAttrib in both images to check if allocations are pinned by default. If not, try using cudaHostAlloc with cudaHostAllocMapped to compare.
perf-bot: profile snapshot stored at /perf/artifacts/1765432100/snap-1.json (nvprof summary + timeline).
sam: Action items: maria to run allocator check and cuobjdump (ETA 2h). akash to create microbench harness for matmul tile shapes and run on both images (ETA EOD). olivia to validate PREFETCH_KV gating and memcopy paths (ETA 3h). ci-bot will run a reproducible CI job across both images and collect nsight traces.
maria: One more note — kernel flags we've toggled in past (TORCH_USE_CUBLASLT=1, CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG) can nudge kernel selection. Documenting them in the loadtest fixture is critical. I'll add a small doc to the playbook.
jit: If we find that driver patch is the culprit, we should pin driver version in our bench infra and add a delta-check in the CI that compares nvcc/cuda/driver version strings before running long tests.
sam: Agreed. For now, let's try to isolate whether memcpy or kernel choice is dominant. If memcpy is root cause we can mitigate by ensuring pinned allocator on hot paths or tweak KV prefetch timing.
olivia: I'll try toggling PREFETCH_KV=false in the repro run to see p99 impact. Will report. :mag: :hourglass_flowing_sand:
sam: thanks all — keep notes in the replay ticket (ENG-RT-4802) and paste short repro commands here when ready.
